steps.what: Select the coffee order and enter the amount on the payment device.
Receive customer payments, handle cash and confirm the tender succeeded.

tasks.design: Test native payment-device integration in the {OTHER} coffee-shop point-of-sale system. Reuse the order amount while the barista continues cash handling, customer help and payment-result checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order total may be keyed separately into a terminal.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported native payment links can transmit that amount directly.
tasks.still_hard: Cash, split tenders and failed payments still require the barista.
tasks.human_edge: Help customers complete payment without losing track of their order.
tasks.altitude: Less amount entry; payment and refund rights stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Payment failure handling and cash policy.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native payment links can remove repeated amount entry, with no claim that customer service disappears.

assumptions: Boundary starts at an agreed coffee-order total and ends at payment completion. Customer tender time and existing authorization runtime are excluded and unchanged.
Till supplies order_id, amount and currency; terminal supplies transaction_id, order_reference and status. Missing integration retains manual entry and result checks; no card credential extraction.
Native configuration first. Central saving assumes some duplicate amount entry exists; already integrated shops use the zero-benefit scenario.
unknowns: Existing payment integration and cash share.
research_questions: Can the terminal reliably identify the correct order during rapid counter service?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=90 gross=10 net=9 after 1 upkeep. Low: integration already used; high: repeated amount entry remains. Physical tender and payment-result checks retain all time.

tasks.short: Take customer orders and convey preparation instructions.

steps.what: Take customer orders and clarify drink size, milk and other preferences.
Record the drink order and check the exact preparation modifiers before sending.
Convey the checked order to employees preparing drinks or food.

tasks.design: Test native drink presets and preparation-ticket routing in the {OTHER} point-of-sale system. The barista keeps the customer conversation, checks the exact size and modifiers, then sends that version directly to the preparation station.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drink modifiers may be repeated verbally or copied onto a second ticket.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets and station routing can reuse the captured order.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual requests and allergy instructions still require direct clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Catch a modifier that conflicts with what the customer actually wanted.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated ticket communication; preparation authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Identify a modifier that needs clarification before starting.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere routes orders through the point-of-sale system to bar or kitchen, according to the digest.
Model knowledge: native drink presets can reduce repeated ticket entry while preserving customer clarification.

assumptions: Boundary ends when the preparation station receives the order; actual preparation remains outside and unchanged. Barista customer conversation retains its full share.

Menu owner supplies drink_id, size_options, milk_options, allowed_modifiers and station_id; barista supplies quantity and special_instruction. Missing modifier codes retain manual clarification; failed routing falls back to a visible manual ticket.
Native configuration first. The s2 review binds checked drink ticket v1, including size, milk, modifiers and special instructions. Any edit invalidates approval before s3 sends.
unknowns: Existing ticket routing and frequency of nonstandard requests.
research_questions: Can preparation staff interpret each modifier correctly without verbal repetition?

already_counted.description: Check the captured drink ticket before sending.

incremental.description: Resolve failed sends and report missing modifier options.

approvals.approved_version: checked drink ticket v1: drink, quantity, size, milk, modifiers and special instructions; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=65 gross=35 net=33 after 2 upkeep. Low: native tickets already used; high: repeated entry and verbal relay removed. Nonstandard clarification is included in upkeep, not transferred for free.

tasks.short: Check freezer, refrigerator and heating-equipment temperatures.

steps.what: Read equipment temperatures using displays or the required manual probe checks.
Compare temperatures with approved operating limits and identify unusual readings.
Inspect suspected equipment faults and alert the responsible lead.

tasks.design: Test native temperature-controller monitoring in the {OTHER} equipment system before installing anything new. Where validated readings exist, use deterministic limits and stale-signal alerts; retain required probe checks, physical fault inspection and human decisions about equipment or food.
tasks.previous_blocker: Temperature checks are distributed across equipment and local instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported controllers can expose readings and timestamps without model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A faulty sensor or normal air temperature does not prove food safety or full equipment function.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a physical fault despite an apparently normal sensor reading.

ambition.what: Investigate a validated refrigerator-temperature excursion between scheduled rounds.

tasks.altitude: Fewer routine display visits where feeds are reliable; no food-release or repair authority is gained.

reach.task: Prepare an equipment-temperature exception for maintenance.
reach.learn: Approved escalation rules and sensor validity checks.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supported temperature-controller feeds and fixed-limit alerts can replace some display reading, with validation and manual fallback.

assumptions: Boundary is equipment-temperature monitoring, not cooking, food-release assessment or repair. The retained 40% of s1 covers manual probes and physical checks; only validated remote display readings lose time.

Equipment controller produces equipment_id, sensor_id, reading, unit, timestamp and fault_state; food-service lead supplies approved_limit, duration_rule and manual_check_schedule. Missing, stale or suspect readings require the original manual instrument procedure.

Test native monitoring first. Central estimate assumes compatible installed controllers; otherwise retain manual work rather than assume free new sensors. Integration includes feed validation, maintenance calibration checks and rollout access.
unknowns: Controller compatibility and which checks require manual probes.
Approved limits, escalation coverage and calibration responsibility.
research_questions: Can the feed detect faults and stale readings without replacing required physical checks?

already_counted.description: Review temperature exceptions and questionable readings.

incremental.description: Handle feed failures and perform added sensor plausibility checks.
Maintain controller access and calibration verification.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=24+12.5+15=51.5 gross=48.5 net=45.5 after 3 upkeep. Low: no compatible controllers; high: validated remote readings for routine refrigeration checks. Manual probes and fault response retain their time.

tasks.short: Describe menu items and suggest appealing choices.

steps.what: Check current menu descriptions, ingredients and product availability.
Describe menu items to customers and suggest products matching their preferences.

tasks.design: Test a native approved-menu register in {DOCS} or the {OTHER} point-of-sale system, linked to current availability. Keep descriptions and preference-based suggestions personal; incomplete ingredient records trigger a question to the food-service lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printed descriptions and actual ingredient changes may diverge.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned recipe records can give staff a common factual source.
tasks.still_hard: Personal taste and dietary uncertainty cannot be resolved by a generic recommendation rule.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt an explanation to the customers tastes without inventing ingredient guarantees.

ambition.what: Explain unfamiliar coffee styles to first-time specialty-coffee customers.

tasks.altitude: Less factual lookup; recommendation and substitution rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Explain preparation differences between two drinks.
reach.learn: Approved recipes and plain flavour language.

evidence.claim: Apicbase stores allergen and dietary recipe data, according to the digest; this supports factual menu records rather than automatic customer suitability decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is menu advice, excluding order entry and preparation. The whole conversation retains its share.

Menu owner supplies item_id, recipe_version, description, ingredients, approved_allergen_information and availability; stock team reports unavailable items. Missing or changed ingredients retain manual source checking and referral rather than inference.
Test native item or recipe views first. No customer profiling or generated allergy assurance is proposed.
unknowns: Menu-record completeness and existing lookup convenience.
research_questions: Can staff distinguish approved ingredient facts from preference advice?

incremental.description: Report stale descriptions and availability mismatches.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=92 gross=8 net=7 after 1 upkeep. Low: familiar menu and complete existing records; high: fragmented descriptions. All customer conversation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native records to cut repeated entry and lookup while keeping customer care and physical food-service checks.
role.ambitious_version: A barista who handles orders accurately and explains choices clearly while noticing equipment or ingredient uncertainty early.
